what: A full-width paper strip covers the space the section occupies and its top and bottom edges are torn — the edge is a jagged line made of five-octave noise (grain .012/px, depth ±35px) with 3px grain ±2.5px layered on top, a bright paper rim (the inner fiber) 9px just outside the tear, and a dark shadow (.35) 60px beyond that. The paper surface has 6% fiber mottling with 2px horizontal·.5px vertical grain. Use it to slot a content panel between sections that have a pinned 3D stage behind — a product news section where an oil-paint stage slips under the torn paper

options.depth: Tear depth (px, half the noise width), default 35
options.shade: Shadow strength (0~1), default .35 — 0 means no shadow
options.full: If on, covers the full screen width even if the element is narrow (default on), if off only the element width
options.seed: Noise seed — different tear per section, default 0

note: Colors are --kf-bg (paper), --kf-surface (inner) and --kf-contrast-bg (shade). The original draws covers at section positions via post-processing over a Theatre scene. Here each part lays its own WebGL plate behind the element (overflowing above and below by depth×2+rim) to produce the same image. Without WebGL, only a --kf-bg face is laid.

from.where: index.html .w-paper (content panel) — the original is the sectionTransition cover from Effects (overlayColor #dcdcd0)
